ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows a single triangle, with the base horizontal, the lower-left angle labeled 51°, the lower-right angle labeled 43°, and the length 103 labeled beside the right slanted side. Reasoning: The sum of the interior angles of a triangle is 180°, so the vertex angle is 180° - 51° - 43° = 86°. The right slanted side 103 is opposite the lower-left angle 51°. Using the sine rule: the other slanted side (opposite 43°) = 103·sin(43°)/sin(51°) ≈ 90.4; the base (opposite 86°) = 103·sin(86°)/sin(51°) ≈ 132.2. Perimeter = 103 + 90.4 + 132.2 ≈ 325.6, rounded to the nearest tenth is 325.6.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a single triangle with bottom-left angle 51°, bottom-right angle 43°, and the right slanted side labeled 103. The text asks for the perimeter rounded to the nearest tenth. First find the top angle by triangle angle sum: 180° - 51° - 43° = 86°. Treat the side labeled 103 as opposite the 51° angle. Use the Law of Sines to find the other two side lengths: side opposite 43° = 103·sin(43°)/sin(51°), and base opposite 86° = 103·sin(86°)/sin(51°). Add these two lengths to 103 and round the sum to the nearest tenth, giving 325.6.
